name: rotation-ruler
title: Rotation Ruler
description: A straighten dial: a ruler of degree ticks slides under a fixed marker and snaps to level.

perf.budget: The tick strip is static views moved by one UI-thread transform; React re-renders once per whole degree.

a11y.reducedMotion: The ruler follows the finger but does not glide after a flick and settles without a spring.
a11y.screenReader: Adjustable role reading "12 degrees"; increment and decrement move by one degree.
a11y.touchTarget: The whole 56 pt panel is the touch area.

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { RotationRuler } from '@/components/kinetik/rotation-ruler';

const [angle, setAngle] = useState(0);

<RotationRuler value={angle} onValueChange={setAngle} />;
<Image source={photo} style={{ transform: [{ rotate: `${angle}deg` }] }} />;
```

## When to use

- Straightening a photo or rotating a layer by small angles.
- Any bounded angle where feel matters more than typing a number.

## When not to use

- Full turns: a ruler of 360 ticks is slow to sweep. Use a dial or 90° buttons.
- Values that are not angles.

## Notes

- A flick glides a little before it settles on a whole degree; resting within two degrees of zero snaps to level.
- Double-tap the ruler to level it. Haptics tick on every degree and land firmer on zero.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add rotation-ruler`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
